title: Week of August 10, 2026: A 7.9% County Levy, Election Day, and Lake Elmo's Fire Station Site
summary:
Washington County's recommended 2027 budget would raise the county levy 7.9% and add $67 to the county share of the tax bill on a median-valued home; polls are open for the state primary; and Lake Elmo's council is asked to reconsider what gets built on the old fire station site.

IN THIS EPISODE
1) Washington County's recommended 2027 budget (presented Aug. 4). Total spending ~$524.7M (vs. $435.0M adopted for 2026, +20.6%, driven by capital outlay +64.5%). Net county levy $148,952,000 -> $160,719,000 (+7.90%). County tax rate 24.45% -> 25.68%. On a home valued at $430,500, the county share goes $1,033 -> $1,100 (+$67, +6.5%) — county only, excluding city, school and watershed. Human-services cost shifts from the state and federal government total $2,868,750 for 2027, less a $307,400 offset = $2,561,350, or 1.71 points of the levy increase; another 0.67 point is held back for county program aid uncertainty and 2028 shifts, for a combined 2.38 of the 7.90 points. Staffing drops 5 FTE to 1,498.69. Capital: $39M facilities, $143M road and bridge, $6M parks. A $40M bond is planned for 2027 — $20M Stafford Library (Woodbury), $11M Park Grove Library, $9M south public works facility.
2) Election Day. Polls open 7 a.m.-8 p.m. Two joint powers agreements with the MN Secretary of State for recount services (2026 primary and 2026 general) were on the county board's Aug. 11 agenda, brought by Elections Division Manager Matt Moore.
3) Lake Elmo's old fire station site. The Tap & Ladder / Machete team, awarded the site by competitive RFP, has asked to keep open a "Plan B" for the restaurant lot — "4 Alarm Fun," a family-oriented arcade and snack bar. Staff say the revised concept "would result in a lower assessed value"; the east portion of the parks building must be demolished. Fiscal impact: "No city expenses tied to today's decision."
4) $20,000,000 in state Local Road Improvement Program funding for the Highway 36 / Lake Elmo Avenue interchange, in three MnDOT grant agreements on the county's Aug. 11 consent agenda. Also: a $182,314 Sunram Construction trail contract on County Highway 14 (34th St. N.) with a maintenance agreement with Oakdale, and a $243,030 historic courthouse elevator replacement, both on the Aug. 4 agenda.
5) Lake Elmo water: a $27,000 MPCA grant (SWIFT contract 294158) for a feasibility study on connecting the 505-unit Cimarron Park to city water, funded under the 3M settlement's conceptual drinking water supply plan. The city also asked residents to cut outdoor watering on Aug. 7.
6) Schools: both boards met Aug. 10 in workshop. The Oakdale-area board (North St. Paul-Maplewood-Oakdale) discussed referendum planning — no amount, date or question language published. The Stillwater-area board reviewed its governance retreat and went into closed session on labor negotiation strategy.

UPCOMING MEETINGS AND HOW TO TAKE PART
- Tue. Aug. 11, 9:00 a.m. — Washington County Board, Government Center, 14949 62nd St. N., Stillwater. Public comment at the start of the meeting; fill out a comment card before it begins. Budget workshops (public works; Gold Line) follow the meeting and are open to the public.
- Tue. Aug. 11 — State primary. Polls open 7 a.m.-8 p.m. Mail ballots accepted at the county's two vote centers until 5 p.m. Register at the polls with proof of residence.
- Wed. Aug. 12, 7:00 p.m. — Oakdale City Council, Discovery Center, 4444 Hadley Ave. N. Open forum, three minutes per speaker.
- Wed. Aug. 12, 7:30 p.m. — Woodbury City Council, City Hall, 8301 Valley Creek Rd., and online at woodburymn.gov/VirtualMeetings. Open Forum: sign up before the meeting; three minutes per speaker, 20 minutes total. Questions: 651-714-3524 or council@woodburymn.gov, 8 a.m.-4:30 p.m.
- Thu. Aug. 13, 3:00 p.m. — Washington County canvassing board (primary results).
- Tue. Aug. 18 — Stillwater City Council regular meeting. Agendas and eComment at the city's Granicus portal.
- Key budget dates to calendar: Sept. 22, county board sets the preliminary 2027 levy; Dec. 1, public budget hearing (after 6 p.m.); Dec. 15, final levy, budget and capital plan adopted.
